ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a benziodoxole-like hypervalent iodine reagent; the benzene ring is fused with a five-membered ring containing I, an intraring O, and a lactone carbonyl; the iodine center is connected to the aromatic ring and the intraring oxygen, and bears three acetoxy ligands, shown respectively as AcO on the left, OAc above, and OAc on the right. On the right side of the figure is an alcohol structure, with the central carbon connected to R1, R2, and oxygen, and the oxygen connected to H; there are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: After ignoring the arrows, the alcohol on the right is not bonded to the reagent on the left, and R1 and R2 are represented with wildcards, giving the general substituted methanol fragment *C(*)O. In the reagent on the left, one of the three acetoxy ligands can be written as the prefix CC(=O)OI1, indicating that the acetoxy group is connected to iodine numbered 1; the other two acetoxy groups are written as branches on iodine as (OC(C)=O)(OC(C)=O). Then the intraring oxygen-carbonyl fragment OC(=O) of the benziodoxole ring where iodine is located is retained, and it is closed with the fused benzene ring as c2ccccc21. Therefore the entire left side is CC(=O)OI1(OC(C)=O)(OC(C)=O)OC(=O)c2ccccc21. The alcohol on the right and the reagent on the left are two unbonded molecular fragments, connected with a dot, giving *C(*)O.CC(=O)OI1(OC(C)=O)(OC(C)=O)OC(=O)c2ccccc21.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First visually transcribe all non-arrow bonds in the image. Encode the right-hand alcohol R1-CH(OH)-R2 as a generic substituted carbinol, replacing R1 and R2 by wildcard atoms to get *C(*)O. Then encode the left reagent: start from iodine in the five-membered benziodoxolone ring as I1, attach two acetoxy ligands as (OC(C)=O)(OC(C)=O), include the cyclic oxygen-carbonyl segment OC(=O), and close onto the fused benzene ring as c2ccccc21. Combine the disconnected alcohol and reagent with a dot, yielding the SMILES expression.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use chemical abbreviation and SMILES conventions: Ac/OAc means acetyl/acetoxy, encoded as CC(=O)O when attached through oxygen; generic R substituents are represented with wildcard atoms '*'; disconnected species are separated by '.'; the benzene-fused iodine lactone ring can be encoded with ring closures as OI1...OC(=O)c2ccccc21 while preserving iodine valence and the two acetoxy ligands.
